title: Real‐Time Visual Sorting of Construction and Demolition Waste Using Low‐Annotation‐Cost Instance Segmentation
content:
MatMatch enables training-free automatic instance-level annotation of construction and demolition waste using SAM2-guided mask generation and DINOv3-based visual prototype matching. Its distilled student model, MatMatch2Real, achieves high segmentation accuracy and real-time inference while substantially reducing the need for manual pixel-level annotations.


ABSTRACT

Construction and demolition waste (CDW) instance segmentation is essential for automated sorting and high-value recycling, yet conventional supervised methods usually depend on large scale pixel-level annotation that are particularly costly to obtain. To address this challenge, this study proposes MatMatch as a training-free automatic instance-level annotation framework for CDW scenes, rather than a deployable inference model. The pseudo-labels generated by MatMatch are further distilled into a lightweight student instance segmentation model, termed MatMatch2Real, for real-time deployment. Specifically, MatMatch first guides SAM2 to generate candidate instance masks through a box-prompting strategy based on the Lab color space and connected-component analysis, then refines the candidate masks via geometric and quality-based post-processing, and finally assigns semantic labels by matching self-supervised visual features extracted by DINOv3 against few-shot category prototypes. Without any additional model training or pixel-level supervision, MatMatch achieves an mAP50:95 of 0.766 and an mAR of 0.816 on the full dataset, substantially outperforming existing automatic annotation baselines. The distilled student model, MatMatch2Real, further achieves an mAP50:95 of 0.863, an mAR of 0.890, and an inference speed of 253.8 FPS. Notably, the student model trained solely on pseudo-labels generated by MatMatch already attains 95.1% of the fully supervised performance. With additional fine-tuning using only 1.6% of the ground-truth annotated images, it reaches a performance level comparable to full-data supervised training. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can generate high-quality automatic instance-level annotations for CDW, substantially reduce the reliance on manual annotation, and support efficient real-time deployment.
